title: The Cessation of Action and the Nature of Resurrection
english: The temple is a tower, in which those approaching were required to offer the fruits of piety to God, all of them fulfilling everything according to the law. Moreover, the altar is a threshing floor upon which the blood of the sacrifices was poured out; the priestly order are farmers, and all those handling this [service], so as to prepare for the people the harvest from the teaching of the law to offer to God with a 'good' 'conscience'.

A prophet speaks of the servants who departed according to the appointed time, those who were sent to make the people or the priests mindful of what is owed to God. For the rebuke was continuous against them, especially against those, more than the rest, who were the causes of the ruin; and they remained enduring all sorts of evils from the Jews, and especially from those who seemed to be in authority among them, without yielding any more. Regarding the Son, he speaks of his arrival (παρουσίαν), having suffered by them and having risen and having destroyed them wickedly (Mt 22:1-14).

This is a wedding of a church being joined to the Word, and a preparation for the wedding through the giving of the gifts of the rich, which is likened to those being prepared for guests in a rich banquet. For Paul says that we are 'in everything' 'made rich' in Christ, 'in word and in knowledge'. The first and second servants are called: the first being those who ran toward the presence of the Lord as fellow-workers and successors of the apostles. But neglect prevents those who are called; for those 'walking according to the flesh' do not follow the divine call toward Christ.

Furthermore, there is the call of the Gentiles, and no longer is there a distinction of race, nor does Israel have the privilege; rather, grace is for those who are negligent and those who are rejected, for 'both the wise and the foolish' as Paul says, and both the evil and the good as the parable says. For he calls those who have taken care of themselves, comparing them to the generally wicked. And the evil may undergo a transition from wickedness, if they entirely obey the good-doing call and 'put on the new man'; but if not this, they were indeed called, but they were not chosen, and indeed their call is overturned; for they are rebuked even for having been convinced of a false entrance. But the ministers who cast out such people are angels. And the binding of feet and hands is...

A cessation of all activity. For no longer is any practice given to the wicked, the time of strangers having been fulfilled in which they have done nothing good. But by saying 'darkness' more externally, he speaks further on of divine virtue and glory.

Regarding the question of those testing [him], as it is recorded (Mt 22:16), witnesses who wished to be present wanted to appear as those most opposed to the true Christ, saying that Christ is of Herod, and as being in authority and able to accuse.

We know, however, that even regarding this word, those from Valentinus and Marcion still contend, bringing the word up to souls; for they say that these live, and have spoken concerning these as being the god of the god of these. But the dispute with the Sadducees was not about souls, but about bodies, so that the answer was about these (Mt 22:23). It is said then that the dead rise, when the soul is with a body, not as if the soul were dissolved in the interval, but as being inactive and lacking the proper things of life which are with a body; for man and life are one thing in common, and both must be reunited toward the life from death.

He did not say 'Lord of the Spirit', but 'of David' (Mt 22:43); for not because he called Christ 'Lord' while speaking in spirit, must the Father be made a slave, as those impious toward the Spirit dare to do. For David says, 'and a son' of the handmaid of God, and this does not yet fit with the [Holy] Spirit, but is said regarding his own spirit. He spoke in spirit, for instance, when he said, 'do not take your Holy Spirit from me' (Psalm 51:11). And 'do not take your spirit from me' did not yet fit with the [Holy] Spirit; for he was not about to take it from himself, nor even when he confessed his sin were those confessions of the Spirit.

Look, that there are not by nature any sons of Gehenna (Mt 23:15); rather, it should be sought whether the Gentiles, before they were baptized, were not sons of Gehenna. Because they marveled at gold, they valued the gold in the temple above the temple, it being necessary not to value the matter, but the name, since the temple was called by the name of God, and the gold was shown to be precious because of the name of the temple (Mt 23:16). And because they profited from the sacrifices because of the gains from them,

title: Wings, Shelter, and the Gathering of the Saints
english: The gift of the altar was more glorified because what was previously placed on the altar as a sheep or a calf or something like that, through the placement upon the altar, was already a gift of God and was called so and was shown to be holy; for the altar was anointed with the oil that sanctifies, and the gift through that received sanctification. Not however in the spiritual things is it thus; for gold in the present temple of God is the Spirit itself, and the body of Christ is the gift upon the spiritual altar. Therefore, the things being put in are greater now than the things receiving; for these indeed sanctify, but those are sanctified.

Through symbols the law taught purity in life. And the custom according to the Jews was such a thing, to cleanse the cups and the vessel of the dish from the ancient traditions, so that they might hold this clean from the touch of sinners and thus avoid the fellowship of sinners, as if they were not even touching the vessels they had touched. But much more they prepared through such customs to flee from sin itself. But those who carefully observed these customs, while themselves seizing and violently gaining profit, became abominations through their works. 'Therefore, flee from injustice, O blind Pharisee, not even seeing what you do' (Mt 23, 25-26), he says; 'and clean to you are the things in the cup and in the dish, if they are not taken through injustice. Much better is the vessel cleansed by righteousness beside the water.'

Those having spiritual wisdom, which Paul says, and scribes who interpret the old things newly, so that the names are the same as with the prophets and sages and scribes of old, but the things themselves are not the same; for neither is the prophecy, nor the wisdom, nor the scribal art about the same things. But he who said 'I will send' showed the divine; for it is God's to send prophets and sages and scribes, the one capable of giving the Spirit of prophecy and wisdom and knowledge.

On account of which he was about to bring wounds upon her because she is a murderer (Mt 23, 37). Therefore he charges her as a murderer; for she, he says, is killing the prophets and stoning those sent to her, and because she, being able many times to receive mercy, was not willing; for it showed many times and many generations...

After He brought the people back from captivity, they were scattering themselves through sins. He teaches the God-befitting thing by speaking of wings and shelter, as it was said by Moses concerning God: 'He received them under His wings' (Ps 91:4); and by David: 'the children of men hope in the shelter of Your wings' (Ps 17:8). For since Satan was scattering them, partly into idolatry and partly into loves of pleasure, He sent prophets, and then came through Himself so as to 'gather' them 'into one.'

But they did not endure to be under His shelter; for He says, 'As a devoted bird, I always had you, drawing you back toward myself, but you did not want to, but were scattering yourself through sinning, casting yourself away from God.' But the bird is motherly and warm in love, caring for the children and giving herself up for them. Therefore, He pre-announces two convergences: one of Jerusalem, the second of the whole inhabited world. And who came in His name? Simon the Magician, saying he was the great power; Mani came; a certain Dositheos the Samaritan came, claiming to be the prophet proclaimed by Moses.

Montanus alone said in his local writings: 'I am the Word, the Bridegroom, the Paraclete, the Pantocrator, I am all things.' He speaks of the wilderness because John lived in the wilderness so much (Mt 24:5); and of the treasuries because Christ was born in a cave and a small hut at the first appearance (Mt 24:26). He says he contrasts the inhabited world with the desolate wilderness through the treasuries (Mt 24:26).

For just as eagles tear at a dead animal to be fed, so when Christ appears, the saints will be drawn to Him (Mt 24:27-28). For it will not be as at the first appearance, moving from place to place through the flesh during the transition, but at the second, His appearance will be manifest to all 'in the twinkling of an eye' (Mt 24:27), like a lightning bolt that does not need to be signaled. And immediately all the saints, having grown wings like eagles, are gathered to Him; for where Jesus fell as a corpse according to the economy of suffering, in order that He might raise those who fell, all will be gathered together, not by chance, but those who...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Nature of the Passover and Christ's Sympathy
english: Disciples bearing wings and having constructed wings according to Solomon. Regarding Matthew 24:27-28, a certain likeness and a parable and an example has been spoken; for just as, when a carcass and a dead body is found lying, eagles and other flesh-eating birds are suddenly lifted up from the unseen to be fed, being carried from those high places through the air, so also, he says, the presence of the Son of Man shall be. For his appearing again upon the earth according to the second and glorious presence to judge the inhabited world, and hosts of angels guarding with spears, shall be manifest, and all the saints, being moved, 'in an instant, in a blink of an eye' (1 Cor 15:52) according to the last trumpet, as the apostle says, just as certain birds, eagles, being swift in movement, shall appear from the unseen; most fittingly being likened to eagles because of thinking the high and heavenly things and being worthy to live the citizenship of the kingdom of heaven. But some have attempted to explain this spoken word in this way, saying that in the second presence of the Lord, all those who have lived justly and, like eagles, are high and heavenly in their mind, will be left behind the parable, and will be gathered to that place where the carcass became of Adam and the transgression of the commandment, through which he fell into sin.

Regarding Matthew 24:31, the Son of Man will send, saying, his angels, God showed the Son of Man; for angels are of God, and to send them is God's own. And that from the ends of the heavens to their ends teaches us the same to be both ends of earth and heaven, so that one must believe in Christ and not be deceived, as the smallest part of the earth is in the midst of the heaven exceeding it in infinite greatness.

Regarding Matthew 25:24, 'Hard,' he says, 'is your command, to seek obedience from men, to whom you did not make the hearing easy through the word. Therefore, fearing that I might become ineffective, I kept only what was for myself, and did not strive concerning others.' 'Hard,' he says, 'is your command, because you seek obedience from men, to whom you have not given the hearing through your word. And because of this, fearing to be ineffective...'

May I become only a person of my own nature, not being unhurried regarding others. Because you involve yourselves, the fault stands around you. The power of things is shown by the impression of the words, as if the righteous were saying these things and as if hearing what the nature of the matter possesses; for it is clear that they would not say these things then, nor would they seek them, when it has been dissolved by the one spoken of by Christ (Mt 25:34). But so often in the words of the scriptures, things lying in the matter are characterized.

But Mark and Luke did not say he had said, 'I will give the Passover,' as he says 'as another,' but 'Where is the lodging, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples' (Mt 26:17-18). These things are able to indicate the 'preparation of the Passover,' not the eating; for John indicates according to the day of the Passover, lest the Passover be eaten by the Jews, since, as we said, it was necessary according to the same day and hour that both the type of Passover and the truth be fulfilled. Nor was it yet intended for the man to indicate that the Passover is being prepared, but before the knowledge of it, it was necessary [to be] Passover, unless even this I noted by saying 'my time is near.'

And he also indicates in that supper that which he himself ate as the supper; for Luke says: 'When it became hour, he sat down, and the twelve apostles with him. And he said to them: With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer; for I say to you, I shall not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God' (Luke 22:14-18). For he did not say again 'I shall not eat it,' but 'I shall not eat,' indicating his sympathy toward the disciples, because he pitied them, as they were going to have the feast unobserved due to his departure; for this is the 'I desired to eat the Passover with you before I suffer,' bringing forth that they shall have sorrow, and he will prefer, over their cheerfulness, that which is profitable to both them and the whole world—not to eat the Passover, but to become himself a Passover, whose fulfillment is 'in the kingdom of God,' when it completely surpasses death; for this is what the word Passover indicates, signifying a surpassing.
The preparation of the Passover has indeed happened. And it is a supper, and not yet the eating of the Passover; for not even...
